4-bit PCM, end to end

Given
  • \(m=2\cos2\pi t+3\cos12\pi t\) (tones at 1 Hz and 6 Hz)
  • 4 bits/sample
Asked
  • (a) average SQNR in dB
  • (b) error at n = 0, 1, 2 (Nyquist sampling)
  • (c) PCM output at n = 0, 1, 2

Spot it: two tones → don't use 1.76 + 6.02n. Find \(m_p\) (sum of amplitudes), the power (sum of \(A^2/2\)), Δ, then snap each sample (moves 5 and 6).

Hint

\(m_p=5\), Δ = 10/16. B = 6 Hz → \(T_s=1/12\) s. Levels \(-5+(k+\frac12)0.625\).

Full solution · every step, with your calculator
Given
  • \(m(t)=2\cos2\pi t+3\cos12\pi t\)two tones: 1 Hz and 6 Hz
  • 4 bits per sample, uniform quantiser over \([-m_p,m_p]\)mid-rise levels, lowest level = 0000
Find

(a) average SQNR in dB; (b) the quantisation error at n = 0, 1, 2 (Nyquist sampling); (c) the PCM codes at n = 0, 1, 2.

Understand it fully · how a uniform quantiser works, slowly

The range \(-m_p\) to \(+m_p\) is cut into L equal steps, each \(\Delta=2m_p/L\) tall. Each step has one output level at its middle ("mid-rise"). Number the steps 0, 1, …, L−1 from the bottom; the code is that number in binary.

To quantise a sample x: (1) how many steps above the bottom is it? \((x+m_p)/\Delta\). (2) Which step is it in? Round down that number (or equivalently round \((x+m_p)/\Delta-\frac12\) to the nearest whole number). (3) Its level is \(-m_p+(k+\frac12)\Delta\). (4) Error = |x − level|, never more than Δ/2. A sample exactly at the top (\(x=m_p\)) would give k = L, so clip it to L − 1.

SQNR = signal power ÷ noise power, with noise power \(\Delta^2/12\). Signal power of a sum of different-frequency tones = sum of each \(A^2/2\).

PCM of a ramp

Given
  • \(s=Kt\) on [0, 1] s, \(s(10^{-3})\lt1.5\) V
  • Uniform quantiser, \(f_s\) = 2000 Hz
  • Error at t = 0 is 0.25 V; at t = 1 ms is 0.05 V
Asked
  • (i) average SQNR in dB
  • (ii) error at t = 0.5 ms

Spot it: the error at s = 0 tells you the levels. s(0) = 0 with error 0.25 → the nearest level is ±0.25 → mid-rise with Δ = 0.5 V (lesson 23).

Full solution · every step, with your calculator
Given
  • \(s(t)=K\,r(t)\) on \(0\le t\le1\) s, 0 elsewherea ramp of slope K
  • \(s(10^{-3})<1.5\) V; sampled at 2000 Hz; uniform quantiser
  • quantisation error at t = 0 is 0.25 V; at \(t=10^{-3}\) s it is 0.05 V
Find

(i) average SQNR in dB; (ii) the quantisation error at \(t=0.5\times10^{-3}\) s.

Understand it fully · reading Δ from an error

At t = 0 the signal is exactly 0. With mid-rise levels, 0 sits exactly halfway between two levels, so its error is the largest possible: Δ/2. So \(\Delta/2=0.25\) → \(\Delta=0.5\) V, and the levels are at ±0.25, ±0.75, ±1.25, …

(i) SQNR
  1. \(N_q=\dfrac{\Delta^2}{12}=\dfrac{0.25}{12}=\dfrac1{48}\).
  2. Ramp power over [0, 1]: \(\displaystyle\int_0^1K^2t^2\,dt=\dfrac{K^2}{3}\).
  3. SQNR \(=\dfrac{K^2/3}{1/48}=16K^2\) → \(10\log_{10}16+20\log_{10}K=12.04+20\log_{10}K\) dB.

The official key prints 28.134 + 20 log K; recomputing gives 12.04 + 20 log K. Show your working so the grader can follow it.

Finding the possible K
  1. \(s(1\text{ ms})=0.001K\) must be 0.05 V from a level (0.25, 0.75, 1.25) and below 1.5 V: \(0.001K\in\{0.2,0.3,0.7,0.8,1.2,1.3\}\) → \(K\in\{200,300,700,800,1200,1300\}\).
(ii) error at 0.5 ms
  1. \(s(0.5\text{ ms})=0.0005K\): K = 200 → 0.10 V → nearest level 0.25 → error 0.15 V; K = 300 → 0.15 → error 0.10 V.
  2. Likewise K = 700 → 0.35 → 0.10; 800 → 0.40 → 0.15; 1200 → 0.60 → 0.15; 1300 → 0.65 → 0.10.
error = 0.15 V or 0.10 V depending on K

Delta modulation: minimum step and SNR

Given
  • \(f_s\) = 64 kHz, \(A_m\) = 1, fmax = 3.4 kHz
  • (ii) signal uniform on [−1, 1]
Asked
  • (i) \(\Delta_{min}\)
  • (ii) SNR in dB

Spot it: "slope overload" → \(\Delta f_s\ge2\pi f_mA_m\). "SNR" → noise after the LPF, \(\frac{\Delta^2}{3}\frac{B}{f_s}\) (lesson 29).

Full solution · every step, with your calculator
Given
  • \(f_s=64\) kHzDM sampling rate
  • \(A_m=1\)maximum amplitude
  • \(f_m=3.4\) kHzhighest voice frequency
  • signal uniform on \([-1,1]\)for the signal power in (ii)
Find

(i) the minimum step \(\Delta_{min}\) to avoid slope overload; (ii) the SNR in dB.

Understand it fully · the staircase must keep up

DM sends one bit per sample: "go up by Δ" or "go down by Δ". In one sample time \(T_s=1/f_s\) the staircase can climb at most Δ, so its fastest slope is \(\Delta/T_s=\Delta f_s\).

The signal's steepest slope (a sine \(A_m\sin2\pi f_mt\)) is \(2\pi f_mA_m\), at its zero crossings. If the staircase is slower than that, it falls behind: slope overload. So we need \(\Delta f_s\ge2\pi f_mA_m\).

When it does keep up, it hunts up and down around the signal: the error is anywhere in \((-\Delta,\Delta)\), uniformly. The mean square of a uniform error on \((-\Delta,\Delta)\) is \(\Delta^2/3\). That noise is spread evenly from 0 to \(f_s\); the receiver's low-pass filter keeps only the part up to B, a fraction \(B/f_s\).

Part (i) · minimum step
\(\Delta_{min}=\dfrac{2\pi f_mA_m}{f_s}\)

\(f_m\)3400 Hzhighest voice frequency
\(A_m\)1given
\(f_s\)64 000 Hzgiven
  1. \(\Delta_{min}=\dfrac{2\pi\times3400\times1}{64\,000}=\dfrac{21\,363}{64\,000}=0.3338\).

Build the DPCM and ADPCM tables

Spot it: each row is the same five steps: guess (previous \(m_q\)) → d → code (which bin?) → \(d_q\) → \(m_q\). For ADPCM, update Δ after the row (lesson 28; the animation there is this table).

Full solution · every step, with your calculator
Given
  • \(m[k]=[0.8,\ 2.1,\ 4.5,\ 7.2,\ 7.8,\ 6.0]\)six samples
  • predictor \(\hat m_q[k]=m_q[k-1]\), \(\hat m_q[0]=0\)first order
  • DPCM step Δ = 1 V; 4-level quantiser: d ≥ Δ → 11 (+1.5Δ); 0 ≤ d < Δ → 10 (+0.5Δ); −Δ ≤ d < 0 → 01 (−0.5Δ); d < −Δ → 00 (−1.5Δ)
  • ADPCM: after an outer code (11/00) Δ × 1.6; after an inner code (10/01) Δ × 0.7Lecture 21 rule
Find

The DPCM and ADPCM tables (codes, reconstruction) and each MSE.

Understand it fully · one row at a time

Every row does the same four things: 1. prediction = last reconstruction \(m_q[k-1]\). 2. error \(d=m-\text{prediction}\). 3. pick the code from where d falls, and its output \(d_q\). 4. new reconstruction \(m_q=\text{prediction}+d_q\). For ADPCM, update Δ for the next row.

DPCM (Δ = 1 throughout)
  1. k = 0: pred 0, d = 0.8 → 10 (+0.5) → \(m_q=0.5\), error −0.3.
  2. k = 1: pred 0.5, d = 1.6 → 11 (+1.5) → 2.0, error −0.1.
  3. k = 2: pred 2.0, d = 2.5 → 11 → 3.5, error −1.0.
  4. k = 3: pred 3.5, d = 3.7 → 11 → 5.0, error −2.2.
  5. k = 4: pred 5.0, d = 2.8 → 11 → 6.5, error −1.3.
  6. k = 5: pred 6.5, d = −0.5 → 01 (−0.5) → 6.0, error 0.0.
  7. MSE \(=\dfrac{0.09+0.01+1+4.84+1.69+0}{6}=\dfrac{7.63}{6}=1.2717\) V².
ADPCM (Δ changes)
  1. k = 0: Δ = 1, d = 0.8 → 10 → \(m_q=0.5\) (error −0.3).Inner → next Δ = 0.7.
  2. k = 1: d = 2.1 − 0.5 = 1.6 ≥ 0.7 → 11 → \(+1.05\) → 1.55 (error −0.55).Outer → Δ = 1.12.
  3. k = 2: d = 4.5 − 1.55 = 2.95 → 11 → \(+1.68\) → 3.23 (error −1.27).Δ = 1.792.
  4. k = 3: d = 7.2 − 3.23 = 3.97 → 11 → \(+2.688\) → 5.918 (error −1.282).Δ = 2.867.
  5. k = 4: d = 7.8 − 5.918 = 1.882 < 2.867 → 10 → \(+1.434\) → 7.352 (error −0.448).Inner → Δ = 2.007.
  6. k = 5: d = 6.0 − 7.352 = −1.352 → 01 → \(-1.004\) → 6.348 (error +0.348).
  7. MSE \(=\dfrac{0.09+0.3025+1.6129+1.6435+0.2007+0.1211}{6}=0.6618\) V² (about 48% lower).

DM of a trapezoid made by convolving two rects

Spot it: rect(width 1) ∗ rect(width 2) = a trapezoid: ramps of slope 1 (height 1 reached over width 1) and a flat top as long as the difference of widths. Ramps decide E; the flat top is where granular noise lives.

Full solution · every step, with your calculator
Given
  • \(m=p*q\): p = rect of height 1 on [−½, ½]; q = rect of height 1 on [−1, 1]
  • DM at \(f_s=4\) kHz
Find

(a) sketch m; (b) minimum Δ; (c) granular noise duration; (d) number of bits; (e) data rate for \(p*q(4t)\) at Nyquist.

(a) the convolution
  1. Widths 1 and 2 → m is a trapezoid: zero beyond ±1.5 s, flat top of height 1 on [−0.5, 0.5], ramps of slope ±1 V/s in between.
(b) minimum step
  1. Steepest slope 1 V/s → \(\Delta\ge\dfrac{1}{4000}=0.25\) mV.
(c), (d)
  1. Granular noise happens on the flat top (the staircase hunts): duration 1 s.
  2. m lasts 3 s → \(3\times4000=12\,000\) bits.
(e) data rate
  1. \(q(4t)\) has width ½ → its sinc main lobe reaches 2 Hz; p's main lobe ends at 1 Hz.The product of the spectra is limited by the narrower: B = 1 Hz.
  2. Nyquist rate 2 Hz; DM sends 1 bit per sample → 2 b/s.
